notable_residents.name: Janis Joplin
notable_residents.detail: Described in the source as "the pink house". No dates given; the same source places Joplin at 122 Lyon Street from June 1967 to April 1968, and notes a competing claim for 112 Lyon Street.

permit_summary.note: Nine of the 22 are street-space or sidewalk occupancy permits (M-prefixed) carrying a nominal $1 valuation; they are omitted from the page timeline. Several alteration permits name individual apartments; unit numbers are omitted here.

narrative.lead: Eight apartments over four storeys on a 2,500-square-foot lot, built the year before the earthquake. A published guide to notable residences names it as a Janis Joplin address and calls it "the pink house".

sections.heading: Three addresses, one tenancy
sections.body: The same guide that places Joplin here also places her at 122 Lyon Street from June 1967 to April 1968 — citing her driver's licence — and records a competing claim for 112 Lyon Street. Three buildings are in circulation for one period of one person's life. None of the three claims has been traced here to a primary source, and this page does not adjudicate between them.

sections.heading: Permit history
sections.body: Nine of the 22 permits on file are street-space or sidewalk occupancy filings at a nominal $1 valuation, omitted here. What remains is a decade-by-decade cycle of apartment rehabilitation, filed in matched pairs, around two jobs that touched the whole building.
